test_title: PYST 13: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 03 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the main purpose of the e-Jagriti platform, launched by the Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India on 1 January 2025?

options.text: To provide a single interface for consumer grievance redressal
To expand India’s space exploration and satellite launches
To manage real estate and government accommodation services
To promote digital payments under the Digital India programme

solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide a single interface for consumer grievance redressal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **e-Jagriti platform** was launched by the **Department of Consumer Affairs**, **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution**, Government of India on **1 January 2025**.
 
• Its primary purpose is to **provide a single interface for consumer grievance redressal**, enabling consumers to raise complaints and track their resolution status seamlessly.
 
• This platform is a step toward strengthening **consumer rights and protection** under the framework of the **Consumer Protection Act, 2019**.
 
• The platform integrates with other consumer-centric initiatives such as the **National Consumer Helpline (NCH)**, mediation services, and consumer awareness programs.
 
• It ensures **transparency, accountability, and efficiency** in addressing consumer grievances, thereby promoting trust between consumers and service providers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Consumer Protection Act, 2019:**

 
 
• This Act replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, and introduced several provisions to strengthen consumer rights.
 
• Key features include the establishment of the **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)** to address unfair trade practices and misleading advertisements.
 
• It also includes provisions for **e-filing of complaints**, mediation, and penalties for false or misleading advertisements.
 
 
 
• **National Consumer Helpline (NCH):**
 
 
• The NCH is a toll-free helpline established to address consumer grievances and provide guidance on consumer rights and responsibilities.
 
• It works in collaboration with various regulatory bodies and state consumer helplines.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Initiative:**
 
 
• The e-Jagriti platform aligns with the **Digital India initiative**, which aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• It leverages digital technology to enhance transparency and accessibility for consumers across the country.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Awareness Programs:**
 
 
• The government conducts regular campaigns to educate consumers about their rights, responsibilities, and the mechanisms available for grievance redressal.
 
• Examples include the **"Jago Grahak Jago"** campaign, which emphasizes consumer empowerment and vigilance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of e-Jagriti:**

 
 
• It simplifies the process of lodging complaints and tracking their progress, reducing delays in resolution.
 
• The platform is accessible to consumers across rural and urban areas, ensuring inclusivity.
 
• It serves as a centralized repository for consumer complaints and their redressal status, enabling better data analysis and policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Consumer Protection (E-commerce) Rules, 2020** were introduced to regulate e-commerce platforms and protect consumer interests.
 
• The government has also launched various apps and portals, such as **UMANG** and **CPGRAMS**, to facilitate citizen-centric services.
